transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korva Coleman.
President Trump has departed Shenzhen, China, where he met with world leaders at an economic
summit.
He also joined a highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin
and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
NPR's Jennifer Pack says it appears the three leaders had different goals for their conversation.
If you ask Xi, he said the trilateral summit has been positive, constructive and fruitful.
But the meeting didn't seem to address Trump's key goal, which was nuclear arms control.
Going into the meeting, Trump had said the three are uniquely placed to reduce the number
of nuclear weapons.
In China's statement after the meeting, it didn't address this, only saying that the
three agreed to talk about reducing nuclear risks and preventing more countries from acquiring
nuclear weapons.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reporting, the U.N.'s highest court, the International Court of
Justice, has ruled Myanmar committed genocide against its Muslim Rohingya minority.
As Anna Holigan reports from The Hague, this is from Myanmar's 2017 military operation.
What the judges found was that the military operations may have been legitimate, but some
elements of them showed that there was genocidal intent.
Half of that was inferred, for them to be sure.
So for example, they pointed to the sexual violence, the brutal rapes of women that were
designed to stigmatize, traumatize and reduce the chances of children being born into that
community.
They talked about the burning down of villages.
Anna Holigan reporting, aid groups have published a 31-page report that scores progress on President
Trump's peace plan in Gaza.
The report identified failings across all categories, that includes how well the ceasefire
is holding and access to humanitarian aid, and Pierre's Ayyab Batrawi has more.
The report by nine aid groups gave a failing grade to the implementation of the past year
of ceasefire in Gaza.
It noted Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,650 Palestinians during the ceasefire,
and that Israeli forces have expanded their occupation of Gaza's territory.
The report said just 49 UN-coordinated trucks carried aid into Gaza in September, with only
2 percent carrying medical supplies.
Israel says Hamas is the main obstacle to improving conditions in Gaza, and that it's
facilitating aid as needed.
The report by aid groups that include Oxfam and Refugees International says countries
should replace the Israeli approval process and military inspections of aid convoys with
an independent, transparent system.
Ayyab Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
Artificial intelligence company Anthropic will start selling shares on the Nasdaq stock
market today.
The company has raised more than $81 billion.
So far, nearly a billion shares have been made available on the market.
Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR.
You're listening to NPR.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has visited Venezuela.
He says he has signed an agreement with Venezuelan leaders to recreate military ties between
both countries.
The Trump administration is working to increase its role in that country.
That's after the U.S. military captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife and
brought them to New York to face U.S. drug charges.
The literary world celebrated the National Book Awards last night.
Writer Abdulrahman El-Gendy won the non-fiction award for his memoir, Huna, but NPR's Andrew
Limbong reports he was not allowed into the U.S. to attend the ceremony.
Huna is a look at the six years El-Gendy spent as a political prisoner in Egypt.
Last week, he published an essay in The New Yorker about how his application for a visa
into the U.S. from Europe to attend the ceremony was denied.
His editor, Helen Tommades, accepted on his behalf and read a statement he wrote, which
ended, "May all borders be abolished, may all prisons fall."
Thank you.
[APPLAUSE]
Hannah Lilith Assadi won the fiction prize for her book, Paradiso 17, inspired by her
Palestinian father, who died of cancer.
The non-fiction book, The Fight of Our Lives, AIDS in America by David Levithan and Gabriel
Duckles won the award for young people's literature.
And Bretton Hillman's Still House in the Desert in Equal Contemplation won the prize
for poetry.
Andrew Limbong and PR News.
Forecasters say significant storms in California and Florida have led to flash flooding watches
and warnings.
Florida's Atlantic coast has gotten heavy rain, so is California's Pacific coast.
There are flood cautions from San Francisco to Los Angeles.
I'm Cora Vekulman, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump departs China after trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi, nuclear arms control unaddressed
International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims in 2017 operation
Aid groups grade Trump's Gaza peace plan failing, citing Israeli attacks and limited aid deliveries
AI company Anthropic begins selling shares on Nasdaq after raising over $81 billion
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visits Venezuela, signs agreement to restore military ties
Abdulrahman El-Gendy wins National Book Award for nonfiction but is denied U.S. entry to attend
Hannah Lilith Assadi wins National Book Award for fiction with Paradiso 17
Flash flood watches and warnings issued along Florida's Atlantic coast and California's Pacific coast
